(1) Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 16.03.2024 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rajkot, (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for short), in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.180 /2020, the appellant -Insurance Company preferred present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short).

sentences.text: Though served, none appears for respondent No.2.

(3) It is the case of the claimant that on 24.01.2020, the claimant was going by his motorcycle bearing NO.GJ-03-HM-6064 and when he reached near the spot of accident, one motorcar bearing No.GJ-03-KC-9799 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the motorcycle of the claimant.
 
 C/FA/247/2025 JUDGMENT DATED  
As a result, the claimant got fracture injuries on his right leg and other injuries on his face.
Therefore, the claim petition filed to get compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- from the opponents.
After appreciating the evidence produced on record, the learned Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,37,985/- along with cost and interest @ 9 %

p.a . (4) Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly appreciating the evidence on record and the Insurance Company is not liable to satisfy the award as offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.

After the alleged accident, complaint is filed after a delay of 8 days and as per medical case papers, the claimant was injured due to fall from the motorcycle and hence, involvement of the car is under the cloud.
Evidence is produced by the claimant himself, which is required to be considered by the Tribunal and failed to consider that the offending vehicle is involved in the accident.
As the car is not involved in the accident, insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

He has further submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in granting exorbitant compensation which is on higher side and required to be slice down on the ground that the claimant having no any future loss of income.

He has also submitted that, the claimant has produced IT returns on record which clearly reveals that after the accident, IT returns for the F.Y 2023-24 below Exh:34 is filed and after the accident, income is increased as there is no actual loss of income, hence, question does not arise to consider 40 % future prospective.
Alternatively, he has submitted that if this Court considers future prospective as it is, in that event, multiplier of 15 would not be applicable.
Hence, he has requested to allow the appeal as prayed for.

sentences.text: (5) Per contra, learned counsel for the original claimant has opposed the present appeal and submitted that the Tribunal has not committed in awarding compensation.
Involvement of the vehicle is proved on record.
Complaint is filed against the driver of offending car.
Chargesheet is filed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/247/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined and same is not challenged by the original opponent No.1.
Merely complaint is filed belatedly is not a ground to refuse the compensation or to believe that the vehicle is not involved in the accident.
He has also submitted that income is proved, ITR is produced on record and Court has to consider whatever the evidence led before the Tribunal and not before the Police or in criminal proceedings.
Even in criminal proceedings, nowhere it reveals that motorcycle was involved.

He has also submitted that merely subsequent income is increased, is not a ground to refuse the compensation and in this regard, Mr. Bhalodi has relied on the judgment of Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain vs Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation (2022 INSC 1264).

sentences.text: Hence, he has requested to dismiss the appeal.

(6) Having heard learned counsel for both the sides and upon perusal of the material placed on record, it emerges that the appeal has been preferred on two grounds, namely: (i) alleged non-involvement of the offending vehicle; and (ii) that the subsequent increase in income disentitles the claimant from future prospects or actual loss of income.

To substantiate the claim, the claimant entered the witness box and tendered his evidence at Exh.17, wherein he has categorically deposed that while he was proceeding from his residence to his garage on his motorcycle bearing registration No. GJ-03-HM-6064, the driver of the offending car bearing registration No. GJ-03-KC-9799,
coming from the opposite direction, drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, resulting in the accident.
During cross-examination by the Insurance Company, the claimant denied the suggestion that the accident occurred due to his own negligence.
The complaint is produced at Exh.30, wherein the specific involvement of the offending vehicle bearing registration No. GJ-03-KC- 9799 is clearly disclosed.
Notably, the driver of the offending car did not appear before the Tribunal, did not step into the witness box, and failed to rebut the evidence led by the claimant.
The original opponent No.2, being the owner of the offending vehicle, has also not denied its involvement.

sentences.text:
Thus, when both opponent Nos.1 and 2 have not disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle,
the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence on record and, applying the principle of preponderance of probabilities, has correctly held the driver of the offending car to be solely negligent.
The contention raised by the Insurance Company that the complaint was lodged belatedly cannot, by itself, be a ground to disbelieve the claim.

Similarly, mere reliance on surmises and conjectures or on the history recorded before the doctor that the claimant fell from the motorcycle is insufficient to disprove the involvement of the offending vehicle.
It is not established that such history was given by the claimant himself.

Even otherwise, to prove non-involvement of the vehicle of opponent Nos.1 and 2, the Insurance Company ought to have examined independent witnesses,
which it has failed to do.
There are no allegations on record suggesting connivance between the claimant and the police, nor is there any material to indicate that a fraudulent chargesheet was filed.

In absence of cogent and convincing evidence, this Court is not inclined to accept the submissions that a false complaint was filed or that a wrong vehicle was impleaded merely on the basis of conjectures.
In view of the above discussion, the evidence led before the Tribunal inspires confidence and has rightly been relied upon.

In this context, reference may be made to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Rajani Sahoo & Ors., reported in 2025 INSC 6, which supports the view adopted by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: (7) So far as the other contention regarding filing of income tax return subsequent to the accident is concerned, the Income Tax Return produced at Exh.35 reflects that the claimant's income has gradually increased.
As per the evidence on record, it appears that the claimant has filed Income Tax Returns showing his income as Rs.3,74,910/-.
The Tribunal has duly considered this aspect and has rightly observed that mere increase in income by itself is not a valid ground to deny compensation.
It is an admitted position that the claimant has sustained injuries resulting in 32% NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/247/2025 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined permanent disability.
Merely because the income of the claimant has shown an upward trend after the accident, the same cannot be a ground to refuse the claim for compensation or future prospects.
If the claimant not sustained such permanent disablement, the possibility of a higher escalation or greater increase in income in future cannot be ruled out.

Considering the nature of his work, skill, and capacity to work,
such disablement is adversely affect his earning potential.
Due to the permanent disablement suffered, the progression of the claimant's income is likely to be curtailed to some extent.

Therefore,
merely because the claimant's income has increased after the accident would not be sufficient ground to deny future prospects, as rise in income may be attributable to various factors and does not necessarily reflect the loss of earning capacity suffered by the claimant.
(8) In view of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has not committed any error in holding the driver of the car solely negligent in causing the accident.
The Tribunal has rightly relied upon the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi v. HRTC, reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819, and Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635.

sentences.text: Therefore, it cannot be said that the Tribunal has committed any error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.28,000/- p.m.

(10) So far as addition of 40 % towards future prospects is concerned, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, and applying multiplier 14 as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.

Compensation awarded under the other heads are also just and proper and hence, no interference is called for.
(11) For the foregoing reasons and observation, no interference is called for in the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, present appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
